headline: Broad regional growth and margin gains lift the outlook
summary_short: Johnson Controls reported fiscal Q3 2026 (our shard label: FY2026 Q2) revenue of $6.614 billion, up 9.3% y/y, with GAAP diluted EPS of $1.23 (+15% y/y) and adjusted EPS of $1.42, as organic sales grew 10% on strength across all three regions.
summary_long: Sales rose 9% to $6.614B (organic +10%), led by Americas (+11%, +11% organic) on Applied HVAC strength and data-center demand, while APAC grew 15% and EMEA was roughly flat on Middle East pressure. Segment margins expanded across all three regions on operating leverage and productivity gains; company-wide adjusted Segment EBITA margin rose to 19.8% from 17.6%. Orders grew 27% organically and backlog reached $21.0B, up 32% organically. Free cash flow was $1.194B; JCI repurchased $635M of stock and paid $245M in dividends. JCI raised FY2026 guidance to ~8% organic growth (from ~6%) and ~$5.05 adjusted EPS (from ~$4.85), and initiated Q4 guidance of $1.55 adjusted EPS.

drivers.explanation: Growth was led by Americas (+11%, +11% organic) on continued strength in Applied HVAC and data-center-driven demand; APAC grew 15% on Product & Systems strength, while EMEA sales were roughly flat, constrained by Middle East conflict pressure.

Segment margin gains across all three regions were primarily driven by operating leverage on higher revenue (Americas), favorable pricing and productivity (EMEA), and productivity plus favorable mix (APAC).
Reported net income growth is partly a comparability artifact: the prior-year quarter included $160M of discontinued-operations income from the divested R&LC HVAC business, absent this year.

Raised FY2026 guidance (organic growth to ~8% from ~6%; adjusted EPS to ~$5.05 from ~$4.85) reflects sustained order momentum (backlog +32% organically to $21.0B) and continued margin expansion, per CEO commentary.
